translationRepairs: (Editor's note: The preface to the Astronomical Treatise in Xue Juzheng's History and the Yongle Encyclopedia are lost in the sources we have, but the chapters on solar eclipses, stellar changes, and related topics survive with their records intact and are fuller than the Heavenly Offices treatise in Ouyang Xiu's New History.)

(Editor's note: The preface to the Astronomical Treatise in Xue Juzheng's History is originally missing from the Yongle Encyclopedia, but the chapters on solar eclipses, stellar changes, and related topics survive with their records intact and are fuller than the Heavenly Offices treatise in Ouyang Xiu's New History.)

《薛史天文志序》《永樂大典》原闕 is the standard reconstruction note that the Xue History Astronomical Treatise preface is originally missing from the Yongle Encyclopedia, not that both works are lost; the proposed after restores that scope while keeping the surviving-sections contrast.
In the fifth year, on dingchou of the eleventh month the moon was eclipsed within the Hare's Head celestial division.
In the fifth year, on dingchou of the eleventh month the moon was eclipsed within the Quail's Head celestial division.
鶉首 is the Jupiter-station Quail Head; Hare's Head invents a wrong station name. The proposed Quail's Head correctly names the celestial division of the lunar eclipse.
In the fifth year, on dingchou of the eleventh month, the moon was eclipsed within the Hare's Head asterism division.
In the fifth year, on dingchou of the eleventh month, the moon was eclipsed within the Quail's Head asterism division.
Same Chinese 鶉首 as r0002; the literal field likewise misreads it as Hare's Head. Quail's Head is the accurate station name for this eclipse locus.
After the third hour several streaks of white vapor followed one another westward until they dispersed after the third watch.
After the third point of the watch several streaks of white vapor followed one another westward until they dispersed after the third watch.

Preceding s0181 dates the omen at 一鼓初; 至三點後 continues that night-watch chronology as the third point within a watch, not a clock hour. Replacing “third hour” with “third point of the watch” corrects the misreading.
By after the third point of the night, afterward there were several streaks of white vapor, one after another streaming west, until after the third drum they dispersed.
After the third point, there were afterward several streaks of white vapor, one after another streaming west, until after the third drum they dispersed.

至三點後 means simply after the third point; “By after … of the night” is ungrammatical and invents a night scope, while 後有 is the separate afterward-existence clause. The proposed literal restores both segments cleanly.
